label: The plan command runs seven named checkpoints and terminates after step 7; step 7 is flagged mandatory_check but its only activities are emitting a closeout status and reminding the operator about a later continuity save.

Step 5 already ends in a self-scored confidence checkpoint: five weighted factors (approach clarity 0.25, risk 0.20, dependency 0.20, pattern alignment 0.15, affected-surface 0.20) produce a percentage with a >=80 / 40-79 / <40 ladder, scored by the same context that wrote plan.md.
Step 5 already runs mechanical validation after the write: validate.sh --strict with a STOP-and-repair rule for template drift, plus example-drift and card-sync guards that report but do not block.

Step 5 already dispatches four fresh subagents in one parallel wave (architecture, feature, dependency, test explorers, each subagent_type context, model opus, parallel true), so a read-back brief can ride the existing wave without a new command, agent definition or file.

That wave is conclusion-free by contract: every explorer prompt ends with Do NOT draw conclusions - just report findings, so a comprehension paraphrase (itself a conclusion about whether the document connects) changes the wave contract rather than extending it.

The command carries a level ladder and a precedent for level-gated ceremony: Level 1 is spec/plan/tasks under 100 LOC, Level 2 adds acceptance-criteria at 100-499 LOC, Level 3 is >=500 LOC with a lazy decision-record add-on, 3+ matches 3, and the rules require a checklist only for verification_level_2_plus.

The rules forbid adding an approval prompt in the autonomous path while confirm-mode checkpoints ask the operator to approve plan.md, so a new check must report into an existing checkpoint rather than introduce its own gate.

Level selection is delegated to recommend-level.sh scoring LOC, file count and risk, with judgment allowed to escalate upward only, so any level-based scaling rule reads a value the command already computed.
